quantity.name: FR angles (onset SP1 / full flexion MFF / cessation SP2)
quantity.definition: flexion angle at the first silent position SP1 (EMG silence begins in flexion), at maximum forward flexion MFF, and at SP2 (activity resumes in extension); Angles from photographs (35 mm camera, 3 m, right side) with skin markers: Trunk angle (TA) = angle between the long axis of the thigh and the line D1 spinous process - hip-joint centre; Hip angle (HA) = angle between the pelvic plane (ASIS-PSIS line) and the thigh axis; Vertebral angle (VA) = angle between the pelvic plane and the line PSIS - D1 spinous process; all as flexion from erect (deg).

title: Gupta 2001: erector spinae silence angles, normal forward bending (25 subjects)
condition: standing, knees straight, bend forward to touch toes and return (10 s), no load

source.sample: 25 healthy young subjects (15 M, 10 F), no back symptoms; weighted task: 11 of the males

protocol.summary: Forward bending to maximum flexion with straight knees and return; repeated twice; 10 s per task.
how_to_simulate: Scale the model to protocol.subject_model (mixed sex; mean 158 cm, 52 kg)
Simulate quasi-static forward flexion with straight knees from erect to full flexion (trunk angle 116 deg relative to thigh line), using the measured hip/vertebral split
Output: the vertebral (and trunk/hip) angle at which the model's lumbar erector spinae (L3 region) activation drops to ~0; compare with SP1; SP2 for the return

subject_model.source: Gupta 2001 Table 1 (as printed: mean height 1.58 m, weight 52.0 kg)

protocol.notes: Surface EMG bilaterally over erector spinae at the L3 spinous-process level ~5 cm from the midline (also abdominals, hamstrings, hip extensors); silence = oscilloscope amplitude dropping abruptly to zero (visual, photograph triggered); no normalisation needed (on/off only). Abstract: SP1 at 57% of max hip and 84% of max vertebral flexion; SP2 at 64% / 88% (Results p.493).

data.x: SP1 as % of maximum hip flexion
SP1 as % of maximum vertebral flexion
SP2 as % of maximum hip flexion
SP2 as % of maximum vertebral flexion

extraction.from: Gupta 2001 Table 3 (normal bending) and Results text p.493 / abstract (% values)
extraction.check_notes: Table 3 compared against the page image (p.494). Text: 'Average maximum flexion was 68.8 (SD 11) for the hip and 57.1 (SD 8) for the vertebrae' matches.

pass_rule.rule: |model - mean| <= 1 SD (angles); for SEM-reported data use SD = SEM x sqrt(n)
